claims.claim: Accepted name Dracaena trifasciata; Sansevieria trifasciata is a synonym.
Arabic names لسان الحماة and نبتة الثعبان are used for this plant.

g.note: No Arabic-language source found in search.

u.note: An Arabic-speaking team member should confirm what UAE customers call it (and add any Gulf names).

claims.claim: Best in bright indirect light; survives low light but grows slowly; a room with no window is too dark.

u.note: Baseline sun-through-glass: tinted tower glazing lowers indoor light, so 'bright indirect' near a window is right.

claims.claim: Bright indirect light; gentle morning sun is fine; avoid harsh midday/afternoon summer sun.

g.note: Sunscorch on Sansevieria is well documented; scorched tissue does not recover.

u.note: Baseline summer-heat, sun-through-glass. Local nurseries recommend shade cloth outdoors.

claims.change: Light fact now allows gentle morning sun (RHS, Missouri Botanical Garden).

claims.claim: Water only when the soil is fully dry; under AC often every 2–3 weeks Apr–Oct and 4–6 weeks Nov–Mar, as starting points adjusted for pot size, material, light and coastal vs inland.

g.note: General guidance is 'when fully dry', typically every 2–4 weeks in growth, monthly or less in winter.

u.note: The exact intervals for UAE AC homes are our estimate. Nursery staff to confirm from customer experience.

claims.change: Intervals reframed as starting points; added coastal vs inland drying and pot-size guidance (RHS: check the soil, not the calendar).

claims.claim: UAE tap water is desalinated and remineralised; mineral content varies. Flush if crust or brown tips appear, or use filtered water.

g.note: Salt build-up from hard water and fertiliser causes brown tips in many houseplants.

u.note: Baseline tap-water (medium confidence: secondary lab figures 150–250 mg/L CaCO3). Wording kept as 'often hard'.

claims.change: Was 'UAE tap water is hard'. Now says it is desalinated and remineralised, so it is often hard. 'Often hard' removed: sources conflict (40–120 vs 150–250 mg/L). Flushing now tied to symptoms.

claims.claim: Use fast-draining cactus/succulent mix or potting soil with perlite/sand 1:1; pot must have a drainage hole; terracotta dries faster.

u.note: Linked products exist in the store.

claims.claim: Feed a balanced fertiliser at half strength monthly Mar–Oct; none Nov–Feb.

g.note: Light feeding in the growing season is standard.

u.note: Indoor AC plants grow through the UAE summer, so the long feeding window fits.

claims.claim: Repot every 2–3 years, one size up; best Oct–Nov or Feb–Apr; wait a week before watering.

u.note: Baseline seasons: repotting in the cooler months.

claims.claim: Division is easiest; leaf cuttings root in 4–8 weeks; cuttings from yellow-edged varieties usually grow back plain green, only division keeps the edge.

g.note: Laurentii is a periclinal chimera; leaf cuttings revert. Division keeps the whole plant, so the edge carries over.

claims.claim: Prefers 15–24 °C; copes with summer heat in shade if the soil dries; protect below 10 °C, especially inland and in colder GCC cities.

u.note: Baseline inland-winter (Raknah -2 °C, Jebel Jais -5.7 °C) and gcc-winter.

claims.change: Added inland UAE and GCC cold-night warning to the winter card, the outdoor fact and the 'live outside' FAQ. The draft said winter was no problem anywhere. Ideal range 15–32 °C replaced by RHS 15–24 °C preferred.

claims.claim: Prefers lower humidity; in humid coastal homes water less often.

u.note: Baseline indoor-ac: UAE AC rooms are not reliably dry (Sharjah study 60.7% RH).

claims.change: Removed 'dry AC air' as a UAE fact in three places. 'Any humidity' overstated (RHS: dislikes high humidity with wet soil). Coastal advice added.

claims.claim: Keep about 1 m from a direct AC vent; cold draughts cause brown tips.

u.note: Baseline ac-vents is low confidence (no source). Staff to confirm the 1 m distance is sensible.

claims.claim: Outdoors in shade; full shade May–Sep; check pots every few days in heatwaves; move between AC and outdoors gradually.

u.note: Shade outdoors is supported by local nurseries; the 7–10 day check interval is our estimate for 41–42 °C days. Staff to confirm.

claims.change: 7–10 day check replaced by 'every few days in heatwaves'; acclimatisation advice added.

claims.claim: Toxic to cats and dogs (saponins); nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea; keep away from pets and young children; call a vet after ingestion.
claims.change: Removed 'drooling', which ASPCA does not list; signs now match ASPCA. Added young children and 'call your vet if your pet eats any'; removed 'usually mild'.

claims.claim: Takes in carbon dioxide at night (CAM); one plant will not noticeably change the air in a room.
Mature, pot-bound plants occasionally flower; small fragrant greenish-white flowers that open in the evening.
Can be kept in water and leaf cuttings root in water; grows slower and less reliably than in soil.

u.note: PlantsWorld sells it as a water plant.

claims.claim: Lives for many years; 30–120 cm indoors by variety; slow growth.

Problem causes and fixes: root rot from overwatering, brown tips from salts/irregular watering/drafts, wrinkling from thirst or root damage, flopping from overwatering/low light, mealybugs (alcohol + neem), fungus gnats from wet soil, slow growth normal.

u.note: Staff to confirm these are the problems UAE customers actually report, and add any missing ones (e.g. from WhatsApp chats).

claims.claim: Popular housewarming, Eid and corporate gift in the UAE; in feng shui seen as protective.

g.note: Feng shui framed as a belief ('seen as').

u.note: PlantsWorld sells Eid, corporate and Mother's Day snake plant gifts; it is the top-selling plant.

claims.claim: A snake plant survives in a windowless room only under bright artificial light that is on most of the day, growing very slowly; in a dark room it weakens.

g.note: Horticultural and office-plant sources agree it survives under fluorescent/LED office light placed close to the plant, growing slowly; no light at all fails. Mostly secondary sources.

u.note: Fits UAE offices and flats with interior rooms lit most of the day.

claims.claim: A snake plant does not noticeably clean the air of a normal room; the sealed-chamber results do not scale to homes.

g.note: Cummings & Waring 2019 review of 196 chamber results: 10–1,000 plants per square metre would be needed to match normal building ventilation.

u.note: Not climate-dependent.

claims.claim: Snake plants do not need misting; water left in the leaf centre can rot the base; wipe dust off with a damp cloth.

g.note: Care sources agree: no misting needed, water standing in the rosette can cause crown rot, wipe dust with a damp cloth.

u.note: Humid coastal homes make standing water in the rosette slower to dry, so the advice holds more strongly.

claims.claim: Laurentii has yellow edges; Zeylanica is dark green with grey-green bands and no yellow edge; Hahnii is a compact rosette; starfish (S. cylindrica 'Starfish') has thick round leaves fanning out; all need the same care.

g.note: UF/IFAS: 'Laurentii' has golden margins; 'Hahnii' is the dwarf bird's-nest rosette. Many plants sold as 'Zeylanica' are S. trifasciata; the trade description (dark green, grey-green bands, no yellow edge) is what customers receive. Starfish is a selection of S. cylindrica (now Dracaena angolensis).

claims.claim: Height is measured from the bottom of the nursery pot to the tip of the tallest leaf; mini/starfish for desks, 50–80 cm for side tables, 100 cm+ as a floor plant.

u.note: PlantsWorld store policy from the support KB (KB006, KB008); research cannot check it.

claims.claim: The plant is the same in both options; the nursery pot is cheapest; a decorative pot arrives fully potted with soil mix, perlite and a drainage layer.

u.note: PlantsWorld store policy from the support KB (KB009–KB011); research cannot check it.

claims.claim: In a decorative pot without a drainage hole, give less water each time so it never collects at the bottom; the drainage layer does not replace a hole.

u.note: PlantsWorld store policy from the support KB (KB010, KB013); research cannot check it.

claims.claim: On arrival: bright indirect light, no direct sun or AC vent, leave it in one spot, check soil before watering (often not needed for 1–2 weeks), don't repot for a few weeks; report damage with a photo on WhatsApp within 24 hours.

u.note: Matches the published Refund policy 3.3: report damage within 24 hours with photos and order number on WhatsApp (+971 4 294 1422) or email. Repotted plants cannot be returned (6), so waiting before repotting also keeps the guarantee.

claims.claim: Our own delivery team delivers (no third-party courier); farther-emirate deliveries may move to a cooler day in June–September; damaged items refused at the door or reported with photos within 24 hours are replaced free.

g.note: The old answer promised air-conditioned vans, a 'Transit Guarantee' and 'replacement or credit'. The published policies name none of these: the Shipping policy says Plantsworld's own team delivers and may reschedule in extreme heat; the Refund policy guarantees healthy arrival and free replacement (equal-value item or refund if out of stock).

u.note: Answer now matches the published Shipping (4, 10) and Refund (3.2, 3.3, 4) policies.

claims.change: Removed 'air-conditioned vans' (not in any policy; KB053 asks the team to confirm) and 'Transit Guarantee … or credit'; now states own delivery team, summer rescheduling, refuse at door or report within 24 hours, free replacement.

claims.claim: Plants vary from the photo (photos are representative); customers can ask for a pre-dispatch photo via the checkout note or WhatsApp with the order number.

g.note: Refund policy 3.1: photos are representative, natural variation is not damage. 'From our UAE nursery' removed: the policy says plants come from trusted growers.
